analysis.title: Asia Open - Double booked
key_insights: US tech rebounded for a second day, with semis lifting headline indices. Breadth and participation stayed weak ahead of hyperscaler earnings and Wednesday's FOMC. Spot VIX fell 5%, and options flow showed buyers of delta for a second straight session from hedge unwinds and new upside positioning.
FOMC straddles have compressed to imply moves of 0.65% for SPX and 1.11% for QQQ. SPX has traded down on 6 straight FOMC days. CTA trigger levels remain in focus for systematic positioning.

The UST curve bear flattened, with 2s up 2bps on thin volume. Citi economists expect an FOMC hold and little guidance from Warsh. In SOFR, the front end has been richening and the market is tactically long the whites but structurally short. Further cheapening is needed before systematic funds act. Citi's David Bieber notes longs remain vulnerable into the FOMC, with recent SFRM7 longs in loss below 95.33.
The $70 billion 5-year auction tailed the 1pm market by 0.4bp at a 4.845% yield. The bid/cover of 2.33 sits at the 36th percentile of the past 12 auctions.

The dollar index reached its strongest level in two weeks. EUR was the weakest G10 currency, down five days in a row, after French consumer confidence fell to 80, a 13-year low. JPY was roughly flat near 157.92, with option strikes at 157.85 and 158.00. Cable fell 0.25% ahead of the UK budget.
UK budget: fiscal headroom is expected at £14-15bn versus £12bn now. Anything below £10bn would be very negative for gilts.
Interbank FX volume was about 30% below average. Net flows favored buying NZD and ZAR and selling NOK and PLN. The Citi trader thinks the RBNZ could lean neutral or dovish tonight.

WTI fell nearly 2% to $100, in line with energy equity weakness. The US and Russia are discussing a return of American companies to the Russian oil market as part of wider talks to end the Ukraine war. Gold fell 1% and silver 0.80%.

BRL positioning is normalizing after Sunday's election. USDBRL is at 5.34 after reaching 5.60 on Monday. Flows were mostly one-way, from offshore custodians buying local assets for EM clients and from exporters.
Israeli exit polls point to a stalemate, with neither party winning a majority. ILS strengthened moderately to 3.054.

AUD September CPI is due at 00:30 GMT. Citi expects headline CPI +0.6% MoM, Q3 inflation at 1.2% with risk toward 1.3%, and trimmed mean at 1% QoQ (3.6% YoY). That would be enough for a 25bp RBA hike in November (house view). Citi's economist says Hauser's comments last week make CPI almost irrelevant for the November RBA, though the details may set how hawkish the decision is. Event jump risk is priced at 30bp.

RBNZ is expected to hike 25bps to 3.00% at 01:00 GMT despite a softer Q3 CPI. Three reasons: higher global neutral rates make the current OCR slightly accommodative, oil is $15-20/bbl above RBNZ forecasts (about 0.4pp added to Q4 CPI if sustained), and the TWI is weaker than RBNZ projections. 3% is likely the terminal rate.
BoT is expected to hold at 1.00% at 07:00 GMT. German GfK consumer confidence for November is due at 07:00 GMT, with Bloomberg consensus at -30.1.
Citi's Chart of the Day, from its Inflation Weekly, argues it is abnormal for core PCE to run stronger than core CPI. A Citi call tonight at 21:00 ET previews US hyperscaler earnings.
earnings_insights: Hyperscaler earnings are due this week. The report gives no figures or estimates, only that a Citi US internet/software client call at 21:00 ET previews Citi's expectations and investor feedback.
